items.title: Show HN: Teaching a 4M-param model to read like a child, with RL and no labels
items.contentSnippet:
I have been really interested in reinforcement learning and had a go at trying to teach a model through simulation to read and speak through experience.
It’s two small networks (~4M parameters total) trained on a MacBook. It passed generated versions of England’s Year 1 Phonics Screening Check (36.6/40, pass mark 32), and the bit I like most is that it taught itself irregular words like “glove” through reading practice. It was given 42 sound slots and the voice learned from transcribed recording

items.title: Show HN: Hashsync – Deduplicate SSH streams against the receiver's files
items.contentSnippet:
On a recent trip, while stuck on spotty hotel Wi-Fi and roaming 5G, I got fed up with how much bandwidth commands like rsync and nix-copy-closure waste.
rsync's delta transfer compares each file only with the file of the same name on the destination (or, with --fuzzy, a file in the same directory), so renamed, moved and copied files are sent in full.
nix-copy-closure can be worse: a rebuilt package gets a new store path, so the whole package is sent again, even when most of its contents haven't

items.title: Show HN: Cb2026, a Rust chess engine that revisits a 2004 world-record project
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I'm Carlos. In 2004 Colin Frayn and I ran ChessBrain, a distributed chess computer that played a game against GM Peter Heine Nielsen using machines volunteered from around the world. It set the Guinness World Record for the largest networked chess computer. Some ideas from that project stayed with me, so I created cb2026 (ChessBrain 2026) to explore them.
cb2026 is a chess engine written from scratch in Rust. It speaks UCI and XBoard, so it runs in En Croissant, Cute Chess, XBoard and sim

items.title: Show HN: Dbprint – Database Context for Agents
items.contentSnippet:
CLI that produces an offline snapshot of a database (DDL, column- and relation-level statistics, values with frequencies), combines it with annotations written by you or an agent, and exposes it as MCP and as a web UI. Works with PG, MySQL, Snowflake, ClickHouse, Databricks, BigQuery.
How to try it:
  uvx dbprint context \
    arboretum.seedbank.germination_trial \
    --purpose query \
    --project https://github.com/jakubro/dbprint/blob/main/docs/format/v1/examples/production/.dbprint.yaml
